memos.headline: S08 and S07 Lead on Trend; S04 Oversold but Broken; S02 Structurally Damaged
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in the universe today. S08 sits just 1.4% off its 52-week high with an RSI of 59.7 and +15.2% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks — this is the cleanest uptrend in the group and I want to own it above its 50-day mean (~259). S07 is similarly strong (+26.6% over 12w, +25% relative strength) though its 50% premium to the 200-day mean and 3.44% ATR make me slightly less comfortable with sizing. S05 is at a literal all-time high with +80% in 26 weeks and RSI 68 — momentum is undeniable but the 14.2% extension above the 50-day and 50% above the 200-day screams exhaustion risk, so I'd wait for a pullback rather than chase. On the downside, S04's RSI of 28.1 and -7.9% vs 50-day mean signal a washout, but the negative relative strength (-8.9% over 12w) tells me this is a broken trend, not a buying opportunity — I'd need a reclaim of the 50-day (~512) to reconsider. S02 is the worst chart in the book: -47.6% drawdown from highs, trading 13.7% below its 200-day mean, with acute 4-week relative weakness of -9% vs SPY.

views.note: Strongest risk-adjusted trend: near 52w high, RSI 60, +15% 12w relative strength; would exit on a close below ~259 (50d mean).
Powerful uptrend with +56% in 26w and +25% 12w relative strength, but extended 36% above 200d mean adds risk; invalidated below ~518 (50d area).
At all-time highs with monster momentum but 14% above 50d and RSI 68 — too extended to initiate; would buy a pullback to ~262 (50d area).
Quiet uptrend just 4% off highs, RSI 53, positive 4w relative strength; low-vol name worth holding above ~115 (50d area).
RSI 28 oversold but trend is broken with -9.8% over 4w and -7.1% relative weakness; need reclaim of ~512 (50d) to reconsider.
Catastrophic -47.6% drawdown from highs, 13.7% below 200d mean — structurally damaged; no entry until price reclaims the 200d.
RSI 40.6, -13% drawdown, negative 12w relative strength of -6.3%; trend is deteriorating and I'd need a reclaim of ~228 (50d) to turn constructive.
Flat at 50d mean with -16% drawdown and -5.4% below 200d; no trend to follow in either direction.
RSI 40 and -7% drawdown but still 7% above 200d; range-bound, need a break above ~308 (50d) or below ~278 (200d) for a signal.
Still well above 200d (+17%) but -13.6% drawdown and 5.18% ATR make this volatile; watching ~186 (50d) for a reclaim before getting constructive.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Dominant Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe. S10 stands out with 62.5% YoY revenue growth, a 56.0% net margin, and only $8.47B in total debt—this is the cleanest earnings profile I can find. S05 is similarly compelling at 34.2% net margin with 33.0% net income growth on 15.9% revenue growth, indicating operating leverage and minimal debt ($14.79B). On the other end, S02 posted a 61.2% YoY decline in net income despite 12.2% revenue growth, compressing net margin to just 2.1% on $80.14B of debt—a classic margin deterioration story I want no part of. S09 is shrinking (-5.2% revenue) with falling profitability (-12.3% net income) and an 8.8% net margin that leaves little cushion. I would need to see margin stabilization in S02 and a return to revenue growth in S09 before reconsidering.

views.note: 62.5% revenue growth, 56% net margin, and minimal leverage ($8.47B debt) represent the strongest durable earnings profile in the universe.
34.2% net margin with 33% net income growth and low debt ($14.79B) signals strong operating leverage and durable profitability.
18.4% revenue growth and 35.7% net margin on manageable $43.21B debt are solid, though 12.5% net income growth lags revenue growth slightly.
$180B revenue with 38.2% net income growth is encouraging, but 11.8% net margin and $55.1B debt leave less room for error at scale.
86.4% net income growth is impressive but $90.68B in total debt is the highest ex-financials in the group; I need to see FCF and capex detail before getting constructive.
31% net margin is healthy but $427.2B total debt (financial-sector balance sheet) makes earnings quality harder to assess from these filings alone.
21.2% net margin and 20% net income growth are respectable, but only 3% revenue growth suggests limited top-line momentum.
9.5% revenue growth is decent but a 6.7% decline in net income and $31.74B debt on $17.6B revenue warrants caution until margin trajectory improves.
Revenue declining 5.2% YoY with net income down 12.3% and an 8.8% net margin on $32.8B debt signals earnings compression I do not want to own.
Net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to a razor-thin 2.1% margin despite 12.2% revenue growth—$80.14B debt amplifies the risk of further deterioration.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact but Sticky 3% CPI and Rising Unemployment Signal a Cautious Slowdown Regime
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing cycle: the upper bound has dropped 75 bp over the past year to 4.00%, with 50 bp of that coming in the last three months alone. However, CPI is running at 3.0% YoY and +0.9% over just three months (roughly 3.6% annualized), which means inflation is not yet at target and could slow the pace of further cuts. Unemployment has risen 30 bp over both 3- and 12-month horizons to 4.40%, consistent with a mild slowdown rather than outright recession. The 10y-2y spread has normalized to +55 bp from near-zero a year ago, and the 10y yield at 4.06% is down 37 bp YoY, which supports duration-sensitive growth equities but limits the upside for bank net-interest margins. A CPI print re-accelerating above 3.5% YoY or unemployment jumping above 4.7% would force me to revisit this call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from falling 10y yields and continued easing cycle; lower rates support valuations.
Defensive staples are attractive in a slowdown regime with unemployment trending higher and uncertain inflation trajectory.
Banks see a positively sloped curve at +55 bp but the easing cycle compresses front-end yields, capping NIM expansion.
Cyclicals face headwinds from rising unemployment and a mild slowdown regime; I lack conviction on a reacceleration.
Energy is macro-ambiguous here—slowdown dampens demand but sticky inflation could support nominal pricing; no strong directional call.
Rate-sensitive sectors like real estate or utilities benefit from the 37 bp YoY decline in the 10y yield and ongoing easing.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S07 and S03 Stand Out Positively While S04, S06, and S10 Flash Negative Signals
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in post-earnings price reactions across the universe this cycle. S07 (+11.6%) and S03 (+9.6%) delivered outsized positive reactions to their Q3 results, suggesting genuine narrative shifts that may still have legs—S03 also filed an Other Events 8-K on 11/20 which could sustain attention. On the negative side, S04 (-2.9%), S06 (-1.9%), and S10 (-3.2%) all saw selling on earnings, with S10's reaction being the freshest (11/19-11/20) and therefore least likely to be fully priced. S08, S09, S01, and S02 all had muted reactions near zero, indicating no strong sentiment catalyst in either direction. I have highest conviction on the extremes—the strong positive momentum names and the fresh negative reaction in S10—while the flat-reaction names warrant patience.

views.note: The +11.6% earnings reaction on 10/29 signals a major positive narrative shift that likely attracts follow-on flows.
A +9.6% earnings pop plus a fresh Other Events filing on 11/20 suggest sustained positive sentiment momentum.
Fresh -3.2% earnings reaction on 11/19-11/20 is only one day old and negative sentiment likely has room to run.
The -2.9% earnings drop combined with a prior management change filing suggests an unsettled narrative.
Negative -1.9% earnings reaction on 10/14 and multiple follow-on filings suggest lingering uncertainty, though the move is now five weeks old.
Modest +2.5% earnings reaction is positive but not strong enough to signal a decisive narrative shift.
Near-flat +0.2% earnings reaction and high filing volume (6 filings in 3 weeks) suggest noise rather than a clear directional signal.
Muted +0.5% earnings reaction and routine follow-on filings provide no strong sentiment edge either way.
Essentially flat -0.4% earnings reaction indicates the market had already priced in the result; no sentiment catalyst.
Flat -0.3% earnings reaction and a string of routine filings including a management change suggest no clear directional tone.

memos.headline: Elevated Policy Uncertainty and Surging VIX Signal Structural Geopolitical Risk Across the Universe
memos.body: I am reading a VIX at 26.42, up 45% over one month and 68% over three months, alongside an economic policy uncertainty index at 312.65 that has surged 76% over three months even as it eased slightly in the past month. This combination points to a geopolitical/policy shock that markets have not yet fully digested—likely tied to escalating trade or sanctions actions—rather than a one-quarter earnings event. HY spreads have widened modestly (+23bp over 3m to 3.17%), suggesting credit markets are beginning to price tail risk but are not yet in distress territory. WTI at $60.07 is down 6.4% over three months, which argues against an energy-supply disruption narrative and instead suggests demand-side concern or supply normalization, reducing the geopolitical premium in energy names. Without granular GDELT event data on specific sanctions or export-control actions, I have moderate conviction at best; a formal escalation in US-China export controls or new sectoral sanctions would shift my views materially.

views.note: Four 8-K filings in six weeks suggest active corporate communication amid policy uncertainty, but without content detail I cannot distinguish positive adaptation from defensive posturing.
Four filings since early October including two recent 8.01 Other Events suggest material developments, but the 76% 3m surge in policy uncertainty warrants caution until content is clarified.

Two filings in October amid a VIX spike of 68% over 3m and widening HY spreads suggest this name faces headwinds from the current policy-risk regime; I would need a de-escalation signal to turn constructive.
A single 8.01 filing on Nov 20 provides no directional signal; the elevated macro uncertainty backdrop keeps me sidelined.
One 8.01 filing on Nov 6 with no detail, combined with a 45% one-month VIX surge, leaves me without enough conviction to take a directional stance.

Reg FD disclosure in late October may indicate proactive investor engagement; if the company has limited China/sanctions exposure, the current risk premium could be overdone, but conviction is low without more detail.
